raw_case_text:
A 42-year-old male presented to the medical emergency department with complaints of weakness and significant weight loss over 1 year. He had episodes of low-grade fever in the past year, for which the patient was treated for pulmonary tuberculosis 2 years back. At present, he was again put on antitubercular therapy (ATT) for the past 1 month; however, no improvement was noted and hence the patient was referred to our hospital. There was no significant family history. On general physical examination, the patient was found to be thin built, pale, and afebrile with abdominal distension. Left submandibular and left axillary lymph nodes were enlarged and measured 1.5 cm in diameter. Mild hepatosplenomegaly was noted, however no fluid thrill could be discerned. Ultrasound abdomen revealed enlarged multiple conglomerate of mesenteric lymph nodes with the largest node measuring 22 mm x 18 mm. Clinical chemistry revealed A:G reversal with total protein of 9.5 g%, albumin of 2.0 g%, globulin of 7.5 g%, and A:G ratio of 1:3.75. Other parameters of liver function test and kidney function test were found to be within normal limits. Complete hemogram revealed pancytopenia with hemoglobin: 6 g%, total leukocyte count: 1800/muL, differential leukocyte count: polymorphs 47%, lymphocytes 51%, eosinophils 1%, monocytes 1%, platelets: 48,000/muL, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 50 mm/h. Peripheral smear revealed the presence of rouleaux; however, no hemoparasite was noted.
Fine needle aspiration cytology was performed on the left submandibular and axillary lymph nodes, which yielded thick aspirate. Smears prepared showed few epithelioid cell granulomas interspersed with discrete and aggregates of histiocytes in a background of reactive lymphoid cells and many plasma cells. Numerous intracellular as well as extracellular amastigote forms of Leishmania species were seen [Figure 1]. In view of strong clinical suspicion, Ziehl-Neelsen staining for acid-fast bacilli (AFB) was also done which came out to be negative. Both polymerase chain reaction for Mycobacterium tuberculosis and AFB culture yielded negative result. Later on, rK39 antigen was also found to be positive. Bone marrow examination (both aspirate and biopsy) revealed a prominence of plasma cells and histiocytes along with infiltration by numerous intracellular as well as extracellular amastigote forms of Leishmania spp. Average parasite density (APD) of 5+, i.e., 10-100 Leishman-Donovan (LD) bodies/field, was noted in the bone marrow aspirate (BMA) [Figure 2]. In view of high APD, the patient's human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) status was evaluated which showed positive serology. Immune status evaluation revealed a low CD4 count; 28/muL (reference range: 400-1600/muL). The patient was started on intravenous amphotericin B along with highly active antiretroviral therapy. Improvement was noted after 14 days of treatment (CD4 count: 36/muL). Subsequent bone marrow evaluations revealed a significant fall in APD and clinical improvement in patient's health; weight gain, improved appetite, and rise in CD4 counts.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 42-year-old male presenting with weakness, marked weight loss, and low-grade fevers for one year.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 1-year history of progressive weakness, constitutional fatigue, low-grade fever episodes, and marked unintentional weight loss. He had received treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis two years prior. Due to persistent symptoms, empirical antitubercular therapy was re-initiated one month prior to presentation without clinical benefit, prompting referral for tertiary evaluation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Pulmonary tuberculosis treated two years prior; empirical antitubercular therapy for the past one month without response. No significant family medical history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Chronic weakness, marked weight loss, low-grade fevers, and abdominal fullness; denies cough, hemoptysis, night sweats, chest pain, or jaundice.

objective.physical_examination: General: Thin built, cachectic, pale, afebrile. Head & Neck: Enlarged left submandibular lymph node (1.5 cm diameter). Axilla: Enlarged left axillary lymph node (1.5 cm diameter). Abdomen: Distended with mild hepatosplenomegaly; no fluid thrill.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete hemogram: Hemoglobin 6 g/dL, total leukocyte count 1,800/microL (neutrophils 47%, lymphocytes 51%, monocytes 1%, eosinophils 1%), platelet count 48,000/microL (pancytopenia), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 50 mm/h; peripheral blood smear showed rouleaux formation without visible blood hemoparasites. Serum biochemistry: Total protein 9.5 g/dL, serum albumin 2.0 g/dL, serum globulin 7.5 g/dL, albumin-globulin ratio reversed (1:3.75); renal and liver transaminases within normal reference limits. Mycobacterial workup: Sputum and aspirate Ziehl-Neelsen stains for acid-fast bacilli negative; Mycobacterium tuberculosis PCR and mycobacterial cultures negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal ultrasound: Multiple conglomerate enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes, measuring up to 22 mm x 18 mm, along with hepatosplenomegaly. Fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of left submandibular and axillary lymph nodes: Granulomatous lymphadenitis with epithelioid cell aggregates, reactive lymphoid cells, prominent plasma cells, and intracellular and extracellular microorganisms. Bone marrow aspirate and trephine biopsy: Hypercellular marrow with marked plasmacytosis, histiocytosis, and heavy intracellular and extracellular microorganism burden.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Newly diagnosed advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection / acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS; CD4 count 28 cells/microL, positive HIV serology) complicated by visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) with generalized reticuloendothelial involvement (lymph nodes, bone marrow, spleen, liver) and severe pancytopenia with hypergammaglobulinemia; recurrent active tuberculosis ruled out.
Diagnostic Confirmation: Visualization of numerous intracellular and extracellular amastigote forms of Leishmania species (Leishman-Donovan bodies) on fine needle aspiration cytology of lymph nodes and bone marrow aspirate/biopsy with an average parasite density (APD) of 5+ (10-100 LD bodies per oil immersion field); positive serum rK39 rapid immunochromatographic antigen. Sputum/aspirate AFB smears, MTB PCR, and AFB cultures were negative.
Plan & Outcome: Ineffective empiric antitubercular therapy discontinued. Initiated on intravenous amphotericin B for visceral leishmaniasis along with highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART). At 14 days of therapy, CD4 count increased to 36 cells/microL, repeat bone marrow evaluation demonstrated marked clearance of LD bodies with dramatic reduction in parasite density, and the patient exhibited substantial clinical recovery with weight gain and improved appetite.
